description: Change, add or remove values and get the data back in its original encoding (hex spacing, base64 alphabet and wrapping, PEM label, gzip header), with every other byte preserved. Edits apply in order; the result is decoded again and checked (REENCODE_VERIFY_FAILED otherwise). Editing signed data (a certificate) invalidates its signature; JWTs are not editable. Paths: protobuf field numbers (1.3[2].4: the third field 3 of message 1), DER child indices (0.0.5), a PEM bundle's block index first, CBOR/MessagePack map keys and array indices (users.0.name), a JWT part then JSON keys (payload.sub), JSON keys and indices inside decoded JSON text (users.37.id). Paths cross formats: 2.0.0.5 is the subject of a certificate (base64, PEM or raw DER) held in protobuf field 2.

alts.description: Max interpretations kept per protobuf LEN field (default 3).

as.description: Force how the innermost decoded bytes are interpreted, when auto-detection picks wrongly.

depth.description: Max nesting of layers and messages (default 16).

op.description: set (default) changes the item at path; add inserts: protobuf PARENT.N appends field N, a new map key, an array index (inserted before it), a DER index (value = one whole element as hex:/b64:); del removes it.

value.description: The new value (not for del), in bytepeel's value syntax: "42" or "-2" for integers, "1.5" or "float:NaN" for floats, "true"/"false", "null", "\"text\"" or "str:text" for text, "hex:0a0b" or "b64:CgM=" for bytes, "sint:-2" for zigzag. Protobuf fields keep their wire type; DER elements their tag.

file.description: Path of a local file to read instead of input (binary files are fine).

in.description: How to read the input (default auto). raw = the bytes as they are.

input.description: The data as text: hex, base64, PEM, a JWT, an xxd or hexdump -C dump, or any nesting of these. Give either input or file.

max_items.description: Max protobuf fields, CBOR/MessagePack values and DER elements decoded in total (default 1000000).

output_file.description: Write the result to this file instead of returning it. Fails if the file exists, unless overwrite is true.

overwrite.description: Allow output_file to replace an existing file.

name: set
title: Edit and re-encode data
